To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have formally defined a visual notation for specifying distributed systems with shared variables, that we have developed an intuitive as well an formal refinement theory for this notation, and that we have implemented a tool that supports both specification and refinement of shared variables interaction diagrams.

(i) SVIDs are an intuitive and visual notation for specifying the requirements for a software system that communicates via shared variables; and (ii) refinement of SVIDs can be used to specify and analyze requirements in a systematic way, and to provide an executable specification of the system.

we define SVIDs as a notation for specifying distributed systems that communicate through shared variables, we define a notion of refinement for SIVD specifications that is based on a formal definition of SVIDs, and we provide a formal semantics of SVIDs that is based on the semantics of MSCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a formal framework for the specification of distributed systems based on shared variables.
the development of SVIDs as a formal notation for the specification of distributed systems with shared variables, with a focus on refinement.
the definition of a specification technique and a refinement notion for shared variables interaction diagrams.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SVIDs are a new, intuitive, visual and formal language for specifying distributed systems that communicate via shared variables and that it is a promising approach for the specification of distributed systems.
SVIDs are a suitable means of expressing and refining shared variables interaction requirements of distributed systems.
SVIDs are a suitable notation for specifying and refining the behavior of distributed real time systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a formal basis for specifying and refining requirements of distributed systems that interact through shared variables.
we provide a notation and a set of refinement rules for specifying and verifying distributed software systems with shared variables.
we define a formal notation to specify the interaction of processes via shared variables, and we provide a formal definition for the refinement relation for this notation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
refinement of SVIDs is not a trivial task and that the refinement relation should be based on a notion of simulation.
, while the refinement of MSCs is a well-understood problem, the refinement of SVIDs is a much more complex problem that requires a careful analysis of the underlying semantics.
